product.name: Critical Thinker's Journey: Voter Edition
product.hero: Structured Nonpartisan Civic Analysis & Ballot Decision Matrix
product.tagline: The methodology for citizens who demand verified evidence over campaign rhetoric.
product.description: Critical Thinker's Journey: Voter Edition provides a structured, nonpartisan 7-step reasoning engine for evaluating candidates, legislative proposals, and ballot referendums. The methodology eliminates partisan emotionalism and replaces campaign soundbites with verified roll call voting records, second-order fiscal modeling, and deterministic civic clarity.

framework_steps.name: Core Values Baseline
framework_steps.subtitle: Rank Top Constitutional and Governance Imperatives
framework_steps.description: Establish the voter's foundational civic principles before evaluating candidates or proposals. By defining prioritized principles first, subsequent candidate evaluations remain grounded in consistent governance standards rather than campaign charisma or media narratives.

imperatives.name: Constitutional Originalism & Civil Liberties
imperatives.description: Strict adherence to enumerated constitutional powers, robust defense of Bill of Rights protections, due process of law, and personal privacy against unwarranted state surveillance.
benchmarks: Protection of First and Fourth Amendment guarantees
Limitation of federal agencies to statutory mandates
Preservation of habeas corpus and procedural due process

imperatives.name: Fiscal Discipline & Debt Containment
imperatives.description: Structural reduction of federal deficits, disciplined budget ceilings, elimination of baseline budgeting expansion, and rigorous auditing of public expenditures.
benchmarks: Enforcement of statutory debt ceilings
Audit of defense and discretionary program expenditures
Prevention of unfunded federal entitlement growth

imperatives.name: National Sovereignty & Border Integrity
imperatives.description: Orderly border enforcement, rule of law in immigration administration, targeted national defense posture, and foreign policy prioritizing domestic stability.
benchmarks: Operational border enforcement and visa verification
Defense spending tied to strategic readiness rather than contractors
Prudent military engagement authorized by legislative declarations

imperatives.name: Free Enterprise & Regulatory Restraint
imperatives.description: Protection of voluntary commerce, reduction of administrative compliance burdens on small business, competitive domestic tax rates, and property rights security.
benchmarks: Cost-benefit thresholds on administrative rulemaking
Dismantling of anti-competitive licensing barriers
Equitable tax structure that avoids capital misallocation

imperatives.name: Federalism & Decentralized Governance
imperatives.description: Reinvigoration of the Tenth Amendment, devolving policy decisions to States and local municipalities where citizens exercise greater oversight.
benchmarks: Reduction of conditional federal grants that bypass State legislatures
Local educational and municipal zoning autonomy
State-level regulatory experimentation

imperatives.name: Rule of Law & Equal Protection
imperatives.description: Impartial administration of justice without selective prosecution, uniform enforcement of statutory criminal laws, and insulation of judiciary from political pressure.
benchmarks: Uniform application of criminal statutes regardless of status
Protection of jury trial rights and appellate review
Separation between investigative agencies and political campaigns

imperatives.name: Public Transparency & Institutional Ethics
imperatives.description: Expedited FOIA compliance, ban on congressional insider trading, real-time disclosure of campaign contributions, and elimination of closed-door omnibus legislation.
benchmarks: Single-subject legislative bill requirements
Public access to legislative text 72 hours before floor votes
Mandatory disclosure of executive regulatory lobbying contacts

imperatives.name: Resilient Infrastructure & Energy Independence
imperatives.description: Strategic development of reliable baseload power, grid security against electromagnetic threats, modern freight transport, and domestic technological capability.
benchmarks: Electrical grid hardened against disruption and cyber intrusion
Diversified domestic energy production ensuring price stability
Maintenance of waterways, freight rail, and interstate corridors

framework_steps.name: Signal vs Noise Filter
framework_steps.subtitle: Distinguish Campaign Rhetoric from Verified Action
framework_steps.description: Filter campaign soundbites, press releases, and attack advertisements against verifiable legislative votes, committee actions, roll calls, and executive appointments. The filter assigns higher evidentiary weight to binding actions while penalizing unsubstantiated political declarations.

sources: Partisan Talking Points & Talking Head Commentary

filter_test_cases.claimed_rhetoric: Pledged complete fiscal conservatism and spending reduction in television ads.
filter_test_cases.verified_record: Voted AYE on $1.7T omnibus spending bill containing 4,200 earmarks (Roll Call #412).
filter_test_cases.evidence_citation: Congressional Record Vol. 169, Roll Call Vote 412

filter_test_cases.claimed_rhetoric: Condemned government surveillance abuse at national campaign town hall.
filter_test_cases.verified_record: Voted NAY on amendment requiring judicial warrants for domestic communications searches under Section 702 (Roll Call #119).

filter_test_cases.claimed_rhetoric: Advocated for healthcare cost transparency and patient choice in policy white paper.
filter_test_cases.verified_record: Co-sponsored and voted AYE on Fair Price Transparency Act requiring upfront procedure cost disclosure (Roll Call #284).

filter_test_cases.claimed_rhetoric: Pledged aggressive deregulation to stimulate local small business hiring.
filter_test_cases.verified_record: Introduced REINS Act companion bill requiring congressional approval for major agency rules exceeding $100M economic cost.

framework_steps.name: Second-Order Outcome Modeling
framework_steps.subtitle: Project 5-Year Budgetary and Legal Horizons
framework_steps.description: Model proposed policies beyond immediate popular intent by calculating downstream consequences across fiscal appropriations, structural deficits, constitutional scrutiny, and compliance burdens over a five-year horizon.

modeling_dimensions.label: Fiscal Trajectory & Outlays
modeling_dimensions.description: Downstream costs including interest service, pension adjustments, and expansion of program beneficiaries.

modeling_dimensions.label: Constitutional & Litigation Risk
modeling_dimensions.description: Exposure to federal preemption challenges, dormant Commerce Clause litigation, or civil rights injunctions.

modeling_dimensions.label: Regulatory Overhead for Small Entities
modeling_dimensions.description: Administrative friction imposed on private actors and local municipal agencies.

modeling_dimensions.label: Secondary Market Distortions
modeling_dimensions.description: Unintended price distortions, subsidy dependencies, or supply contraction.

proposals.title: Statewide Commercial Rent Control Act
proposals.first_order_intent: Intended to reduce commercial lease prices for urban small merchants.

projections.key_event: Commercial lease freeze begins; initial federal constitutional challenges filed by property trusts.
Commercial building maintenance deferrals surface; legal defense fund drawn from municipal budget.
Commercial building starts fall 34%; capital migrates to neighboring jurisdictions.
Municipal commercial property tax receipts drop $140M; retail space vacancy in prime corridors.
Legislature forced to consider emergency commercial property tax hike or repeal rent controls.

proposals.title: Clean Energy Grid Transition Mandate
proposals.first_order_intent: Mandate 100% renewable generation within 6 years to curb emissions.

projections.key_event: Initial bond issuance for transmission lines; utility rate case filings requesting 8% hike.
Early retirement of natural gas peaker plants; reserve generation margins shrink to 4%.
Summer peak electricity prices surge 42%; industrial manufacturers curtail peak operations.
Battery storage supply bottlenecks trigger rolling brownout warnings; emergency fossil imports contracted.
Cumulative retail utility rates 68% higher than baseline; taxpayer subsidies required to backstop utility credit rating.

framework_steps.name: Candidate Stance Comparator
framework_steps.subtitle: Calculate Weighted Alignment Scores Across Candidates
framework_steps.description: Evaluate candidates through deterministic weighted scoring. Each candidate's verified position across key civic domains is multiplied by the voter's core value weights from Step 1, producing an objective alignment percentage that reveals substantive compatibility without partisan spin.

candidates.name: Candidate A: Marcus Vance
candidates.title: Constitutional Conservative & Fiscal Realist
candidates.profile_summary: Prioritizes spending caps, statutory deregulation, strict constructionist judicial philosophy, and decentralized municipal control.

stances.rationale: Consistent record defending First Amendment association rights and Fourth Amendment warrant standards.
stances.verification_source: Roll Call Votes 2021-2025; Judiciary Committee Record

stances.rationale: Voted against continuing resolutions without offsetting budget rescissions; authored zero-baseline review amendment.
Supported border physical barrier funding and mandatory employer E-Verify enforcement.
Sponsored legislation eliminating occupational licensing reciprocity restrictions.
Advocates block-granting federal welfare programs to State administration with zero federal mandates.
Supported mandatory minimums for violent felonies and qualified immunity protections for peace officers.
Co-sponsored 72-hour bill inspection rule; moderate disclosures on campaign finance.
Favors private concession models and expedited NEPA permitting over direct federal grant outlays.

candidates.name: Candidate B: Elena Rostova
candidates.title: Technocratic Institutionalist & Infrastructure Advocate
candidates.profile_summary: Prioritizes public capital modernization, institutional regulatory oversight, green energy subsidies, and multilateral alliances.

stances.rationale: Supports federal hate speech guidelines and firearms background licensing expansion.
Voted for all supplemental appropriations bills; advocates raising corporate tax brackets to fund deficits.
Favors international treaty structures and targeted refugee processing expansions.
Supports mandatory ESG disclosures for publicly traded firms and prevailing wage covenants.
Backs national educational curriculum standards and federal zoning preemption for housing.
Emphasizes restorative justice sentencing reform while maintaining federal civil rights enforcement.
Pioneered agency open-data portal; supported lobbying registry enhancements.
Authored $85B regional passenger rail bond and public water filtration recapitalization act.

candidates.name: Candidate C: Dominic Thorne
candidates.title: Decentralist Reformer & Digital Privacy Champion
candidates.profile_summary: Prioritizes digital civil liberties, sound money, elimination of federal surveillance programs, and aggressive judicial restraint.

stances.rationale: Uncompromising defense of end-to-end encryption, digital privacy rights, and Second Amendment protections.
stances.verification_source: Roll Call Record on FISA Reauthorization

stances.rationale: Voted against every omnibus spending package; introduced bill prohibiting Federal Reserve digital currency.
Strictly non-interventionist foreign policy; supports constitutional declarations before military deployment.
Advocates complete tax exemptions for capital gains on domestic manufacturing and software.
Authored legislation abolishing federal department grant conditions and restoring state primacy.
Advocates strict limits on civil asset forfeiture and elimination of non-statutory federal crimes.
Introduced legislation mandating complete public disclosure of all unclassified federal grant audits.
Favors private utility deregulation and nuclear microreactor licensing over public trust bonds.

framework_steps.name: Ballot Referendum Stress Test
framework_steps.subtitle: Test Propositions Against the 5-Pillar Vulnerability Matrix
framework_steps.description: Subject proposed citizen initiatives, bonds, and constitutional amendments to rigorous structural scrutiny. The 5-pillar stress test flags hidden fiscal liabilities, litigation risk, and open-ended administrative discretion before voting.

stress_pillars.name: Constitutional & Statutory Authority
stress_pillars.fail_condition: Exceeds municipal or state police powers, triggering immediate federal court injunctions.

stress_pillars.name: Dedicated Revenue vs Unfunded Mandate
stress_pillars.fail_condition: Appropriates mandatory outlays without dedicated, verified revenue offsets.

stress_pillars.name: Secondary Market Disruption
stress_pillars.fail_condition: Induces housing shortages, supply friction, or flight of private productive capital.

stress_pillars.name: Bureaucratic Rulemaking Discretion
stress_pillars.fail_condition: Delegates unconstrained regulatory discretion to unelected advisory boards.

stress_pillars.name: Sunset Clause & Mandatory Audit
stress_pillars.fail_condition: Lacks automatic expiration (5-7 years) and mandatory independent legislative audit.

propositions.title: Proposition 201: Regional Rapid Transit Bond ($4.8 Billion)
propositions.ballot_summary: Authorizes the issuance of $4.8 billion in general obligation bonds for light rail expansion, funded by a 0.5% county sales tax surcharge.

pillar_evaluations.notes: Clearly falls within municipal bonding and transport authority.
Sales tax revenues assume 3.5% ongoing economic expansion; downturn creates general fund debt burden.
Sales tax increase disproportionately increases consumer goods friction on lower-income households.
Construction oversight assigned to existing transportation authority with statutory procurement rules.
Tax surcharge remains permanent even after bond retirement; lacks required 10-year sunset clause.

propositions.title: Proposition 202: Parental Educational Choice Accounts
propositions.ballot_summary: Permits state per-pupil education funds ($7,800/student) to follow enrolled students to accredited private, parochial, or homeschooling programs.

pillar_evaluations.notes: Conforms with state supreme court precedent and First Amendment freedom of association.
Revenue neutral; funding redirects existing formula funds without net state tax increases.
Fosters competitive dynamics among educational providers without supply restriction.
State education board may attempt regulatory curriculum controls on independent academies.
Mandates annual state auditor general review and 6-year legislative performance reauthorization.

propositions.title: Proposition 203: Municipal Energy Authority Eminent Domain
propositions.ballot_summary: Authorizes municipal government to condemn and seize investor-owned electric utility assets to establish a city-managed power authority.

pillar_evaluations.notes: Invites immediate federal Fifth Amendment Takings Clause litigation and bond covenant defaults.
Understates condemnation valuation by an estimated $1.2B, creating unfunded municipal debt liability.
Triggers immediate municipal bond rating downgrades and utility investment departure.
Grants unelected municipal power commissioners unchecked rate-setting power without judicial review.
Contains zero audit provisions or sunset mechanisms.

framework_steps.name: Trade-off Equilibrium Calculator
framework_steps.subtitle: Calculate Civic Equilibrium and Detect Cognitive Dissonance
framework_steps.description: Evaluate non-zero-sum and zero-sum trade-offs across four governing tensions. The calculator maps personal trade-off positions and alerts the citizen when stated policy desires are mathematically incompatible with fiscal or constitutional limits.

tradeoff_dilemmas.title: Individual Liberty vs Public Security
tradeoff_dilemmas.description_left: Strict warrant limits, encrypted communications, absolute Fourth Amendment protections, minimal administrative enforcement.
tradeoff_dilemmas.description_right: Expanded police authority, automated public surveillance, expedited administrative detention, enhanced border interdiction.

tradeoff_dilemmas.title: Fiscal Austerity vs Public Capital Outlays
tradeoff_dilemmas.description_left: Zero debt expansion, restricted public borrowing, lower corporate and personal tax rates, privatization of public works.
tradeoff_dilemmas.description_right: Large-scale public transit bonds, subsidized clean energy projects, expanded public research facilities, higher progressive tax rates.

tradeoff_dilemmas.title: Market Deregulation vs Precautionary Standards
tradeoff_dilemmas.description_left: Rapid business formation, minimal environmental permitting delays, market-driven wage clearing, unrestricted technological deployment.
tradeoff_dilemmas.description_right: Stringent carbon mandates, strict zoning oversight, mandatory corporate compliance disclosures, aggressive consumer safety vetting.

tradeoff_dilemmas.title: Decentralized Federalism vs Standardized Uniformity
tradeoff_dilemmas.description_left: Policy experimentation by States, localized school governance, regional zoning sovereignty, elimination of federal strings.
tradeoff_dilemmas.description_right: Uniform national commerce standards, centralized educational baselines, federal energy transmission rules, nationwide statutory codes.

dissonance_rules.trigger_condition: High Fiscal Discipline Priority in Step 1 (weight >= 8) combined with high Public Capital Outlays in Step 6 (slider > +20)
dissonance_rules.alert_message: Voter established high priority on Fiscal Discipline & Debt Containment in Step 1, but favored aggressive Public Capital Outlays in Step 6. Public capital investments require debt issuance or tax increases that contradict debt containment objectives.

dissonance_rules.trigger_condition: High Constitutional Liberty Priority in Step 1 (weight >= 8) combined with high Public Security in Step 6 (slider > +20)
dissonance_rules.alert_message: Voter ranked Civil Liberties as an apex priority in Step 1, but selected aggressive Public Security measures in Step 6. Expansion of state surveillance and expedited detention inherently constrains Fourth Amendment protections.

framework_steps.name: Deterministic Civic Clarity Card
framework_steps.subtitle: Deterministic Ballot Digest and Print Preview
framework_steps.description: Generate an auditable, deterministic ballot decision digest. The Civic Clarity Card summarizes prioritized values, verified candidate alignment scores, referendum stress test verdicts, and trade-off equilibrium indices in a high-density, printable layout.
export_features: JSON data export for permanent citizen records
